s1.syndrome_frame: Acute monocular vision loss with orbital and adnexal signs
salient_findings: Pain, numbness, and erythema of the eyelids and forearm
Tense eyelid edema, chemosis, and corneal haze
key_facts: Obese man in his mid-30s
No prior systemic or ocular disorders
Heavy alcohol consumption the night prior
Took 2 buprenorphine hydrochloride/naloxone hydrochloride pills
Denies any trauma
Visual acuity: No light perception in right eye, 20/20 in left eye
Intraocular pressure: 37 mm Hg in right eye, 21 mm Hg in left eye
Creatinine level: 2.2 mg/dL
Creatine kinase level: 29,320 U/L
Periorbital soft-tissue swelling on noncontrast computed tomography
Severe disorganization of the retinal architecture on Optical Coherence Tomography

Tolosa-Hunt syndrome variant with orbital involvement

shortlist.label: Rhabdomyolysis-induced vision loss
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated creatine kinase level and vision loss

shortlist.label: Compressive optic neuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Increased intraocular pressure and vision loss

shortlist.label: Purtscher retinopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Vision loss and retinal changes after trauma or compression

shortlist.label: Orbital compartment syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Periorbital soft-tissue swelling and vision loss

shortlist.label: Ischemic optic neuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Vision loss and relative afferent pupillary defect

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with vision loss, tense eyelid edema, chemosis, and elevated intraocular pressure in one eye, combined with periorbital soft-tissue swelling on CT and severe retinal disorganization on OCT, is most consistent with orbital compartment syndrome. The elevated creatine kinase level and creatinine level also suggest rhabdomyolysis, which can contribute to compartment syndrome.

rejected.label: Rhabdomyolysis-induced vision loss
rejected.why: While rhabdomyolysis is likely present, it does not directly explain the patient's vision loss and orbital findings.

rejected.label: Compressive optic neuropathy
rejected.why: This diagnosis is possible but does not account for the full range of orbital and retinal findings.

rejected.label: Purtscher retinopathy
rejected.why: This condition typically follows trauma, which the patient denies.

rejected.label: Ischemic optic neuropathy
rejected.why: This diagnosis does not explain the patient's orbital findings and elevated intraocular pressure.
